source.title_on_document: CoQuest: Exploring Research Question Co-Creation with an LLM-based Agent

supplement.where: Appendix A, pp. 22-25 of this PDF
supplement.holds: Post-session survey items (A.1, Table 3); mixed-effects model of user feedback length, including coefficients and standard errors (A.2, Table 4); LLM agent prompts (A.3). No additional creativity-outcome statistics. No separate supplementary material is mentioned.

paper_design_summary: Twenty HCI researchers (graduate students or recent graduates) each used the CoQuest LLM agent to co-create research questions under two AI designs, breadth-first (three questions at once) and depth-first (three questions in sequence), one design per task, with the order of designs and topics randomly assigned. Participants rated at least six AI-generated research questions of their choice per task on novelty, value, surprise, and relevance during the task and rated the system after each task; the paper also counts the questions generated.

studies.label: Within-subjects user study: breadth-first vs depth-first CoQuest

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of the two CoQuest designs (breadth-first, depth-first) and of the two task topics, counterbalanced
assignment.quote: we followed a counterbalanced design [57] by randomizing the experiment conditions so that all possible orders and combinations were randomly assigned to an equal number of participants.

arms.name: Breadth-first
arms.description: Each generation produces three follow-up RQs in parallel at the same level; user picks and gives feedback each turn

arms.name: Depth-first
arms.description: Each generation produces three RQs in sequence, each building on the previous one without user input (more AI initiative)

participants.who: HCI researchers from 8 institutions; all graduate students currently enrolled or just graduated, with prior research experience; sessions run remotely over video calls
participants.quote: we conducted a within-subjects user study with 20 HCI researchers from 8 different institutions
participants.locator: p. 8, Section 6; p. 9, Section 7.1.1 ("In total, 20 participants created 504 RQs throughout the study")

ai_tool.name_model: CoQuest agent (AutoGPT/ReAct prompting on OpenAI gpt3.5-turbo-16k; text-embedding-ada-002 for paper retrieval)
ai_tool.how_used: Agent generates research questions from the user's initial idea and typed feedback, shows related papers and its rationale (AI Thoughts); the user picks, rates, and refines the questions

task.description: Co-create research questions with the agent on two topics: "AR/VR for education and learning" and "AI and crowdsourcing", one topic per design
task.duration: Studies lasted 1-2 hours, including two tasks, a survey after each task, and an exit interview

outcomes.name: Participant rating of RQ novelty (5-point Likert, rated during task on at least six RQs per task)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Participants' own ratings of at least six RQs of their choice per task, using 5-point Likert sliders (p. 9, Section 6.2.1). Table 1 reports a separate linear regression for each rating item, with Condition (Depth-First=1; breadth-first=0), Feedback Length, Total # of RQs Created, Acted During Wait, and Familiarity as predictors (pp. 14-15, Section 7.3). The regression sample size, analysis unit, and standard-error basis are not stated; unit=rating describes the collected scores, not a confirmed regression observation unit.

contrasts.reported: MANOVA on RQ ratings F(4, 209) = 3.79, p = .0057**, Wilk's Lambda = 0.909; Mann-Whitney novelty U = 2199.5, p = .002**, d = .40, Power = .89; depth-first (M=3.78, SD=1.29) vs breadth-first (M=3.28, SD=1.22) [this one M/SD pair follows both the novelty and surprise tests; the text does not say which rating it describes]; Table 1 linear regression: Condition (Depth-First=1), β (S.E.) = 1.53 (.63)*; *: p < 0.05. Other predictors are Feedback Length, Total # of RQs Created, Acted During Wait, and Familiarity. Regression sample size, analysis unit, and standard-error basis are not stated.
contrasts.locator: p. 10, Section 7.1.2; p. 15, Table 1; p. 14, Section 7.3 (regression specification)

eligibility.reason: Randomized, counterbalanced order of two generative-AI configurations in a within-person experiment meets criterion 1 (p. 9, Section 6.1). Only 20 people were analyzed, below 50, so criterion 2 is not met and core eligibility is no (p. 8, Section 6; p. 9, Section 7.1.1). Novelty, surprise, value, and relevance are participants' own ratings of AI-generated RQs (p. 9, Section 6.2.1), and fluency counts questions generated with CoQuest (p. 9, Sections 6.2.3 and 7.1.1). Whether these participant self-ratings and AI-generated question counts satisfy the output criterion remains unclear. This small randomized experiment belongs in the screening report; it does not fit a context class.

one_line_finding: With 20 HCI researchers, RQs from the depth-first design got higher participant ratings for novelty (U = 2199.5, p = .002, d = .40) and surprise (U = 2387.5, p = .017, d = .32) than breadth-first (p. 10, Section 7.1.2), while the post-task survey rated breadth-first more creative (M = 3.78 vs 3.18, U = 288.0, p = .015; pp. 9-10, Section 7.1.1).
notes: The code_url points to the CoQuest system implementation, not identified analysis code (p. 2, Abstract; p. 8, footnote 5). For S1-O3, statistics_available=["none"] means that none of the listed complete statistic packages is confirmed: arm means and SDs are printed, but their per-condition analysis n is not separately stated. Those descriptive numbers remain in reported (p. 9, Section 7.1.1). The Table 1 regression observation unit and standard-error basis are not stated (pp. 14-15, Section 7.3). The post-task creativity survey combines a rating of generated RQs with how creative participants felt, so it is retained only in one_line_finding rather than added as an output-only outcome (p. 22, Table 3).
